savvit.name: Savvit
savvit.subtitle: / Visual bookmarking
savvit.summary: I am independently extending Savvit into a visual bookmarking workspace for images, ideas and useful links. The full application supports private, public and selectively shared boards with signed-in discovery. I have also built a standalone browser demo that anyone can explore without an account.
savvit.contribution: I have extended pin uploads, metadata editing, search, saved references and moving owned originals between boards, alongside likes and threaded discussions. I have also added light, dark and system themes, saved appearance preferences, labelled forms and keyboard dialog focus management.

savvit.background: I started from our collaborative university web application, where I worked on authentication, MySQL-backed functionality and module testing. The original team work remains credited in the repository history.
savvit.status: My interactive demo supports sample boards, pin creation, search, likes, comments and saved references. Changes stay in your browser; Reset demo restores the samples. It does not use real accounts, shared permissions or MySQL. End-to-end verification of the full app against real MySQL remains outstanding.

search.name: Mini Search Engine
search.summary: I have developed our university C++ search engine further with a WebAssembly demo that returns ranked results. I can search the sample collection or import local files without uploading their contents.
search.contribution: I have extended the browser experience with local file import and match snippets. The engine combines a positional index, trie-based prefix search and TF-IDF ranking, with phrase and left-to-right Boolean queries.

farm.name: Grid-Based-Farming Game
farm.summary: I rebuilt our university farming game as a C++17 idle game using raylib. I can plant crops, hire workers, buy land and improve yields in the desktop game and the playable browser demo below.
farm.contribution: I rebuilt the game with deterministic production, crop automation, generated artwork and synthesised audio. On desktop, I added saves and up to eight hours of offline production: automated plots earn income while manual crops only mature.

farm.background: Our collaborative OOP project, GridFarmGame, inspired this independent rebuild. I credit the original team and its history in the linked predecessor; I did not copy its code, sprites or audio into this version.
farm.status: The browser demo is session-only. Closing this player, refreshing or closing its tab resets the farm; browser saves and closed-tab earnings are not available.

mergesort.name: Parallel Merge Sort
mergesort.subtitle: / Operating systems
mergesort.summary: I worked with Jeremy Nguyen and Marko Bogsav on a university operating systems assignment in C. We implemented sequential merge sort and a parallel version using POSIX threads.
mergesort.contribution: We divide the array into independent ranges, join worker threads before merging and use a recursion cutoff to switch to sequential sorting. If thread creation fails, that range falls back to sequential sorting.
mergesort.background: I developed this as part of our university team, working through recursion, memory management and thread synchronisation. I retain our shared authorship and the course context in the source documentation.
mergesort.status: Our test harness checks ordering; it does not independently prove that every input element is preserved. I do not claim a measured parallel speedup.
